after.title: Reserve Bank of India: Supersession of Board of Directors of Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd., Mumbai - Extension of period
after.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India, in exercise of its powers under Section 36AAA read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, had superseded the Board of Directors of Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd., Mumbai (the bank) for one year on November 24, 2023, due to material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank. The period of supersession was extended for a period of one-year, effective November 24, 2024 and further extended for a period of one year, effective November 24, 2025.
2. Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026.
3. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in exercise of its powers under sub-Section (1) of Section 36AAA read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, has extended the period of supersession for a further period of one-year, effective from November 24, 2026. Consequently, Shri Satya Prakash Pathak shall continue as the Administrator of the bank and shall be assisted by the present Committee of Advisors comprising of Shri Venkatesh Hegde, Shri Devendra Kumar, and Shri Suhas Gokhale.
(Brij Raj)
Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/1473

after.summary:
Data on sectoral deployment of credit by non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) for the month of September 2026, collected from major NBFCs and housing finance companies (HFCs), are set out in the Statement 1 .
On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, NBFCs’ credit registered a growth of 15.4 per cent in September 2026 as compared to 13.3 per cent a year ago.
Highlights of the sectoral deployment of credit by NBFCs for the month ended September 30, 2026, are given below:
Credit to agriculture and allied activities recorded a robust growth of 17.8 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 as against 5.2 per cent a year ago.
Credit growth in industry sector declined to 7.4 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 as compared with 10.2 per cent in September 2025. Within industry, credit growth in ‘infrastructure’ remained subdued.
Credit growth in services sector moderated to 17.3 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 from 23.0 per cent a year ago. While credit to ‘commercial real estate’ marked buoyant expansion, ‘trade’ and ‘transport operators’ segments also witnessed higher credit growth.
Retail loans growth accelerated to 21.9 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 compared to 16.8 per cent a year ago. Within retail sector, ‘housing loans’, ‘loans against gold jewellery’ and ‘vehicle loans’ witnessed accelerated credit growth.
Ajit Prasad
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)
Press Release: 2026-2027/1461

As part of the ongoing effort towards consolidation of various instructions issued from time to time, the Reserve Bank has undertaken a review of the extant guidelines relating to Priority Sector Lending (PSL) and proposes to issue Directions on the subject RE-wise.
2. Accordingly, the following draft Directions are being placed on the website for public comments:
Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Priority Sector Lending – Targets and Classification) Directions, 2026
Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Priority Sector Lending – Targets and Classification) Directions, 2026
Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks – Priority Sector Lending – Targets and Classification) Directions, 2026
Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Priority Sector Lending – Targets and Classification) Directions, 2026
Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks – Priority Sector Lending – Targets and Classification) Directions, 2026
3. Further, instructions which have not been included in the consolidated draft Directions would be repealed consequent to the issuance of the Directions. The same will be notified separately.
4. The comments / feedback may be submitted on or before November 26, 2026, through the following channels:
i. The ‘Connect 2 Regulate’ section on the website by following the corresponding hyperlink provided against each document in the page where they are hosted.
or
ii. by e-mail with the subject line ‘Feedback on [full name of the draft Direction / (including the type of Regulated Entity)]’.
(Brij Raj)
Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/1447
